scope: Independent review of the UI Cancel checkpoint-freeze repair, preserved Pause assertions, real-worker before/after reports, and final related 18-case browser result. No production edits or browser runs were performed by reviewer.
expectedSemantics: UI Cancel immediately stops the live clock and unlocks controls while retaining the last fully validated state already committed by the UI.
Messages queued from the superseded run, including progress, completion and the cancellation acknowledgement, cannot move that state or overwrite its durable/exportable checkpoint.
The existing UI resume target remains available after Cancel; a new explicit operation may replace it. The next manual 10-second step uses the frozen 10-second checkpoint and reaches 20 seconds.

Direct worker cancellation continues to return its latest validated worker checkpoint. The UI is intentionally free to discard that later acknowledgement under its separately documented freeze contract.

implementationAssessment.reason: invalidate now always advances request identity once beyond its cancellation request. Prior run replies fail the epoch check; a cancellation acknowledgement in the new epoch fails the request-ID check before accept/persist executes. Removing invalidate(true) makes Cancel use the already-established Pause invalidation semantics. Real worker delivery is asynchronous, so invalidation finishes before an acknowledgement handler runs.
implementationAssessment.sourceScope: Only useTwin.ts cancel/invalidation behavior changed. The new test reuses an extracted native Worker message-hold fixture; it does not fabricate simulated output or replace the real solver.
